newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TIMOR PROTEST IN SYDNEY
Dozens of recent arrivals from East Timor are protesting outside the Federal Court in Sydney, against being deported to Portugal.
The Court is reviewing a tribunal's decision to refuse refugee status to a man who was born in East Timor in 1973, when the country was a Portugese colony.
The Immigration Department argues Kim Koe Jong and more than a thousand other recent arrivals from East Timor are Portugese citizens and not eligible for refugee status.
The protesters, who've lit candles outside the court, say they have no link with Portugal.
STUDENTS DELAY MINISTER'S MEETING
Student protesters have sent their union president to look for the Education Minister, Amanda Vanstone, saying she's failed to show for a meeting with university heads in Sydney.
This morning's meeting between the minister and university vice-chancellors has been delayed indefinately with about 60 students inside a city hotel.
They want to confront Senator Vanstone over changes to HECS.
Police have confiscated the protesters' whistles and are refusing to let media into the building.
A representative of the National Union of Students says they just want the minister to hear their concerns.
PRISON ESCAPEE HUNTED IN WA
A police taskforce has been established to search Western Australia for a man who'd escaped from prison in Queensland, while serving a long sentence for armed robberies.
Forty-six year old Alexander McDonald, who escaped from Borallon prison a year ago, is known as one of Australia's most wanted men.
McDonald gained notoriety in the late 1970s in Western Australia when he was convicted of bombing a hotel in the south-west town of Collie.
HOWARD BACKS CARR ON HSC
The Prime Minister has bought into a row about the Higher School Certificate system in New South Wales, and has supported his political rival, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr.
John Howard has supported the use of external examinations. This followed a submission by the Parents and Citizens Federation to the HSC review which advocated downgrading the role of the exams.
HARRADINE KEEPS UP ABORTION PRESSURE
Independent Senator, Brian Harradine, has stepped up his campaign against Medicare funding of abortions and in-vitro fertilisation, and financial assistance for family planning clinics.
Senator Harradine has asked health department officials before a Senate budget estimates committee whether aborting a foetus diagnosed with Down's Syndrome would be appropriate.
Officials say it is a matter for state law, and it isn't possible to say to what extent this practice occurs because the reason for the abortion doesn't appear on the Medicare form.
The Federal Government says there are no plans to change the current system regarding abortion and Medicare.
WORLD INTEREST IN ABORIGINAL ROCK ARTIFACTS
Scientists around the world are re-thinking the origins of the human race in light of the discovery of Aboriginal rock artifacts more than 100,000 years old in northern Australia.

A team from Wollongong University and the Australian Museum has discovered rock art more than sixty-thousand years old, and artefacts 116,000 years old, in the far north-west of the Northern Territory.
Dr Paul Tacon from the Australian Museum says there's been some scepticism expressed about the age of the finds, but the main reaction has been excitement.
He says the discovery has sparked debate and archaeologists and other scientists all over the world are asking fundamental questions about our past.
NSW CRACKDOWN ON DETENTION LEAVE
The New South Wales Government is tightening the rules for people sentenced to periodic detention, in the wake of a series of leave approvals.
Corrective Services Minister Bob Debus has ordered an immediate inquiry after it was revealed that a detainee, Tony Kirby, was granted leave so he could sail in the Sydney to Hobart yacht race.
The minister announced new provisons for periodic detainees after another man broke his detention order by going to the Gold Coast for a holiday.
Mr Debus says the inquiry will look into all approvals for leave granted by the Deputy Director of Periodic Detentions.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
